FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1, and it fails the test A1 states: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer; if it does, the packet states it, and only where nothing establishes it may a named checkable authority stand in. THREE held records establish it, and they agree. The committed route census's destination for this exact route key is name 'Circuit or district court in the county of arrest', detail 'The county-of-arrest venue rule is separate from the general venue rule' — a record that goes out of its way to warn that this route's venue is NOT the ordinary one. The compiled Arkansas profile, named as a requiredSourceId for this route and the very record the fee repair correctly leaned on, carries the filing rule 'File in the circuit or district court that handled the case.' The committed packet-set manifest's file entry says 'File the ACIC arrest petition and order pair in the circuit or district court in the county of arrest.' WHAT THE PACKET SAYS INSTEAD. It never uses the words circuit or district as the answer set, never states the county-of-arrest venue rule, and hands the determination to the participant: 'the court blank is left to you… Write the court that handled the case — or, for an arrest that was never charged, the court that would have handled it — in the county named in the caption… If you are not certain which court that is for your arrest, ask the circuit clerk's office of the county named in the caption.' For a route whose defining fact is that no charges were ever filed, 'the court that would have handled it' is a guess, and the packet's fallback is a phone call about something the repository answers. This is A1's consequence paragraph almost word for word: naming an authority is what honesty requires when the record is empty; it is not a way to avoid stating what the record contains. WHAT THE PACKET DOES WELL, and the repair should keep: the county is prefilled, the clerk's office is named as where the filing is received, and the DIVISION blank is correctly explained as conditional. The repair is one sentence — say that the petition goes to the circuit or district court in the county of arrest, keep the clerk as the authority for the residual circuit-versus-district choice, which genuinely varies. A participant with records in more than one county is therefore owed a separate filing in each, and this packet never says so. A3 also sharpens why the census's rule is the operative one for THIS pathway: the profile's 'file in the circuit or district court that handled the case' is written for a case that WAS handled, while situation-a is defined by no charges ever having been filed, which is why the packet has to reach for 'the court that would have handled it'. The census entry keyed to this exact route key answers that directly — 'Circuit or district court in the county of arrest', with the explicit warning that 'the county-of-arrest venue rule is separate from the general venue rule'. That is the route-addressing record, and it is the one the packet does not state.

The committed route census names that profile as requiredSourceIds[0] for this exact route key, which is what makes it the repository under A2 rather than merely a file that exists. The packet states the answer outright — 'There is no filing fee for this petition' — instead of naming an authority to ask, which is exactly the correction A2 called for on this family. It then does something better than the standard requires: it reads the petition's paragraph 3, a sworn statement that fees 'mandated by A.C.A § 16-90-1419' have been paid, and explains why that averment is true as printed where no fee is required, so the participant is not left signing a sentence they do not understand; and it keeps a named checkable authority for the residual case ('If the clerk … nevertheless asks you to pay something … ask the clerk what the charge is for and whether a waiver or reduction is available, and settle it before you sign'). It also separates the costs that are not filing fees — the ACIC record fee, the clerk's copy fee for a Judgment and Commitment Order, counsel — and names the free legal-aid and clinic route. RECORDED, and it does not change the score: the committed packet-set manifest says 'The source review does not state a filing fee for this petition' and 'The source review does not address a fee waiver', so two held records disagree in strength. One is silent and one answers; A2's instruction is to state what the repository establishes, and the profile establishes it. Stating $0 is right. APPLIED A3 (read from the captain head; it postdates this row's base), because this PASS rests on a compiled state profile and A3 was written about precisely that. A3's test: name the fact and its route, then find the record that establishes THAT fact for THAT route, and refuse a line keyed to a different statutory section. The fact is the filing fee for a petition to seal an arrest under Act 1460 of 2013, A.C.A. § 16-90-1401 et seq. The Arkansas profile's packetGenerator.feeRules is a flat jurisdiction-wide list rather than a per-pathway table, so I checked it for the California shape and it does not have it: every fee line in it gives the SAME answer and attributes it to the SAME Act — feeRules[0] 'Act 1460 eliminated sealing filing fees', feeRules[1] 'Sealing petition filing fee $0 Filing fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments', and the filing rule 'Act 1460 eliminated filing fees for sealing'. There is no competing statutory section and no competing amount anywhere in the list, so there is no wrong line available to pick. The profile declares three pathways — situation-a-non-convictions, situation-b-misdemeanor-convictions, situation-c-felony-convictions — and Act 1460 is the Act all three arise under and the Act this packet's own petition is captioned to ('PETITION TO SEAL ARREST UNDER ACT 1460 OF 2013; A.C.A.16-90-1401, Et. Seq.'), which I read off the delivered fixture. The line addresses this route. The PASS stands under A3.

SERVICE.detail: The recipients and the method are stated correctly and sourced; the DEADLINE is denied, and the repository holds it. WHAT IS RIGHT. The packet names both recipients — 'the Prosecuting Attorney for the County in which the Petition is filed, or the City Attorney — whichever office prosecuted, or would have prosecuted, the case' and 'the arresting agency' — and the method, 'by placing a copy in the United States mail, postage prepaid, or by hand delivering a copy'. I extracted page 3 of the canonical fixture and both come straight off the form's own Certificate of Service, word for word. It also gets the timing discipline right: complete the certificate 'after — and only after — you have actually served both', because 'a signed certificate of a mailing that never occurred is a false statement to the court'. WHAT FAILS. The packet then says: 'The form sets no separate service deadline: the certificate is part of the petition you file, so service belongs with filing.' The claim about the FORM is true. The claim it invites the reader to draw about the RULE is false, and this is A2's exact defect shape one obligation over. The committed packet-set manifest's serve_party entry for ar-arrest-seal-set reads: 'Serve the prosecuting attorney WITHIN THREE DAYS OF FILING. The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object.' A2's answersVT8C4 settles that a committed manifest's participantActionRequired entries are a held source for SERVICE by name. So the repository sets a three-day service deadline and a thirty-day objection window, and the packet tells the participant there is no separate deadline and says nothing about the objection window at all — a participant who reads this will not know when to expect an objection or that one is coming. Repair: replace the no-deadline sentence with the three-day rule and add the thirty-day objection window; keep everything else, which is good. STRENGTHENED UNDER A3. Re-reading the profile per fact rather than per document turned up a second held record on the objection window, in packetGenerator.filingDestinationRules: 'Serve the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 30 days (misdemeanor) or 90 days (felony) to file a notice of opposition stating reasons.' So the repository holds the window twice — flatly as 30 days in the packet-set manifest, and class-dependent as 30 or 90 days in the profile — and the packet states neither. I do not resolve which figure governs an arrest that was never charged, because the packet's own paragraph 1 asks the participant for the offence class and the two records are keyed differently; that is a question for the repairer and, if the records genuinely conflict for this pathway, for counsel. What is measurable and what I score is that the participant is told nothing about an objection window at all, and is affirmatively told there is no service deadline when the manifest sets one at three days.

vfdRead.environmentLimits: This container mounts two of the five source custodies named by the committed corpus index — master_library and human_source_returns — and does not mount d_source_packs or nationwide_recovery_pool_2026_09_02. All six families are zero-binary compositions (CUSTOM_PLEADING_FROM_CODIFIED_TEXT) that bind only committed repository records, so no obligation was NOT_MEASURABLE_HERE for want of corpus bytes. Separately, 14 of the 351 master_library entries the index declares are absent from the mounted tree (Alabama, California, Missouri, North Carolina and Utah forms); none belongs to any family read here, and this is recorded as an environment fact about this container rather than a defect in any packet.
falsePositiveTrapsChecked: Route-key footers were matched after collapsing all whitespace, because these families wrap the footer across lines and a per-line match reports it absent. Footers are per-component, printed on the last page of each component, not per-page; a per-page expectation would have reported dozens of false absences.

The Nevada proposed_order carries no route footer by deliberate design (scripts/build-census-v1-nv_seal_probation_family-set.mjs:311 omits it for that component alone, so the court's own order carries no internal route string). It was checked in the builder before it could be reported as a missing footer.

Repeating-row groups were computed by importing the repository's own rowKeyOf rather than by pattern-guessing, specifically to avoid the known failure in which statutory numerals inside identifiers are parsed as row-group counts. All six families produced 0 row groups; no spurious group appeared from 1017_1019, 1017a, 1018, 19c or 12-60.1-02.
